title: Loop Closure Audit

requirements.statement: Expired evidence must produce executable refresh commands and a scheduled dispatcher must run those refresh workflows without human memory.
Claim-bound code, tests, docs, and reasoning must co-change so agents cannot merge semantic drift after skipping documents.
Harnesses increase exploration space, and failures must become closed-loop candidates instead of isolated artifacts.
Observation, hypothesis, change, verifier, evidence, decision, and next-loop links must be machine-checkable.

residual_gaps.observation: Some claim bindings still rely on files and verifiers while leaving one or more observe, verify, or failure-token coverage arrays empty.
residual_gaps.risk: Agents can infer co-change files, but may still miss why a claim observes or fails without reading adjacent context.

residual_gaps.observation: Harnesses publish closed-loop candidate artifacts, but adoption still depends on fresh candidate decision evidence staying visible to the next agent.
residual_gaps.risk: A failed harness can create a candidate, yet the adoption step can become stale or invisible if agents only inspect the source PR.

loop.observation: Riido has loop registry, evidence graph, harness promotion, and pre-commit gates, but the high-level human-exit objective is still distributed across many artifacts.
loop.hypothesis: A loop closure audit can compile the human-exit objective into machine-checkable requirements that point at existing loops, claims, workflows, hooks, providers, and graph edges.
loop.execute: Verify the required loops, claim bindings, pre-commit hook, scheduled refresh dispatcher, provider harness coverage, harness promotion edges, and evidence graph chains; generate this reader and publish audit evidence in CI.
loop.evaluate: The verifier fails when any human-exit requirement loses its executable proof surface, including missing claims, missing provider coverage, missing scheduled dispatch, missing pre-commit hook, missing graph chains, or stale generated docs.
loop.retrospective: This keeps the objective executable: agents can ignore the prose, but the audit still proves whether the loop system lets humans leave the inner loop.

assertions: loop closure audit evidence must expose each requirement's check details, not only check kinds
